newsitem.title: UK: Britain's GrandMet denies it lost Smirnoff brand name in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Britain's GrandMet denies it lost Smirnoff brand name in Russia.

text.p: British drink and food giant Grand Metropolitan Plc on Monday denied it had lost control of the Smirnoff vodka brand name in Russia, saying it was currently appealing all court decisions against it.
"To suggest this is the end is not true. It is just not the case. It is an interim judgement and we continue our operations unaffected by this arbitration court decision," said a GrandMet spokesman.
An article in Britain's Guardian newspaper said the company had lost control of the brand after a court victory by descendants of the Russian Smirnoff family.
But the market seemed to ignore the report as Grand Met's shares stood six pence higher at 568p.
"This is a long running legal battle in Russia. There are two strands of court action we are following. One in the arbitration courts and one in the civil courts," said the GrandMet spokesman.

In May, a Russian arbitration court judgement ruled against Heublein, GrandMet's U.S. subsidiary, which sells around 15 million cases of Smirnoff vodka around the world including one million in Russia.
The Russian business paper Kommersant Daily reported at the weekend the Moscow Regional Arbitration Court had ruled against the use of the Smirnoff brand name in favour of its Russian rival.

"But contrary to what was in the press this was an interim arbitration judgement. We will appeal it and it will go to a supreme arbitration court in due course. while this process is going on we will continue our operations in Russia as normal," said the spokesman.

The company has also appealed against two decisions made against it in the civil courts at Krymsk and Krasnodar two years ago, both were also brought by former KGB agent Boris Smirnoff, a great grandson of Peter Smirnoff, supplier of vodka to the last tsar.

GrandMet says Hueblein bought the rights to the Smirnoff name in 1933 from an American businessman who had acquired them shortly before from Vladimor Smirnoff. GrandMet also faces a lawsuit in a Delaware court from Boris Smirnoff asking the court to declare void all GrandMet's U.S. trademarks.
"The vast majority of the Smirnoff family work with Hueblein and IDV (GrandMet's spirits arm) on a number of projects in Russia," said the GrandMet spokesman.
GrandMet is currently trying to consummate a 24 billion pound ($39.2 billion) merger with Guinness, the largest in Britain's corporate history. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
